hypotheses.title: Systematic Market Decoupling and Tail-Risk Normalization
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Equities decoupling from systematic market correlation (ts_av_diff(correlation_last_60_days_spy, 60) < 0) while experiencing subdued institutional options crash skew (-ts_zscore(implied_volatility_mean_skew_60, 60) > 0) represent prime unhedged idiosyncratic accumulation candidates. Cross-sectional subindustry neutralization isolates genuine asset-specific mispricings free from macroeconomic factor drag.
confounders: Systemic market-wide liquidity crunches forcing correlation spikes
Binary event risk (e.g. biotech FDA trial outcomes) distorting implied skew
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if market-decoupling equities underperform during broad macroeconomic consolidation regimes.

candidates.rationale: G1/G2/G3+ zero-collision alpha uniting Model51 rolling SPY correlation dynamics with Option8 implied volatility skewness.

hypotheses.title: Higher-Moment Return Asymmetry and Intraday VWAP Dislocation
hypotheses.economic_rationale: The third standardized moment of returns (ts_skewness(returns, 60)) reflects lottery-ticket preference and crash asymmetry. Negatively skewed stocks earn a substantial volatility risk premium. Interacting negative return skewness with short-term price dislocations relative to VWAP ((close - vwap) / vwap) captures institutional execution absorption where temporary intraday dips in high-risk-premium names yield strong mean-reversion.
confounders: Persistent structural bankruptcy risk causing sustained negative skewness
Regime shifts in intraday algorithmic execution flow
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if negatively skewed equities with intraday VWAP discounts continue downward drift without mean-reversion.

candidates.rationale: Pure higher-order statistical moment interaction with volume-weighted price dislocation, completely free of boilerplate templates.

hypotheses.title: Idiosyncratic Risk Surge and Price Reversal Synergy
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Spikes in unsystematic variance relative to systematic variance (unsystematic_risk_last_90_days / systematic_risk_last_90_days) signal idiosyncratic event overreactions. When paired with negative price momentum relative to the 60-day moving average (-ts_zscore(close / ts_mean(close, 60), 20)), this identifies stocks that have temporarily suffered excessive panic discounting and are poised for sharp post-event reversion.
confounders: Permanent impairment of corporate fundamentals driving justified idiosyncratic risk expansion
Prolonged secular bear market in individual sectors
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if idiosyncratic risk expansion indicates fundamental solvency deterioration rather than temporary dislocation.

candidates.rationale: Orthogonal risk-model shock structure exploiting the low-beta/idiosyncratic variance anomaly paired with intermediate trend reversion.
